summary: A Java command-line program on picocli, built with Maven into one runnable jar with config files, exit codes and JSON output.
description: Write a Java command-line program with picocli subcommands and Maven. Settings layer from defaults, a TOML file, environment variables and flags, and every failure maps to a fixed exit code with a suggested fix. Results print as text or one JSON document, logs go to stderr, and the build shades every dependency into one jar that runs with java -jar. The build formats code, catches nullness bugs at compile time, enforces a coverage floor and tests the packaged jar. One config command proves the wiring; the recipe adds no product commands, release pipeline or native binary.
seoDescription: A Java CLI recipe on picocli and Maven: layered TOML config, exit codes with suggestions, text or JSON output, one runnable jar and tests against it.

projectExamples.title: Team deployment helper
projectExamples.description: Illustrative: subcommands that read a shared TOML settings file and print JSON for scripts. Calls to real deployment systems are work the project still has to add.

projectExamples.title: Data file checker for a JVM team
projectExamples.description: Illustrative: a command that checks files and exits with a distinct code per problem, run in CI with the jar. The checking rules are custom work.

plain.whatItIs: A starter for a program written in Java that people run by typing commands in a terminal, with settings files and clear error messages.
goodAt: Internal tools for teams that already work in Java
Commands that other scripts call and read JSON from
Shipping one file that runs anywhere Java is installed
notGoodAt: Instant start-up: each run starts a Java runtime first.
Graphical apps or full-screen terminal interfaces; use another stack.
